answer: A network can resist Sybils with a mutual-credit graph: an agent's rewards are capped by credit lines other agents extend to it, and every line is backed by the extender's own stake. If a credited agent is later judged fake, the extender's stake is slashed too, so vouching is costly and honest agents vet carefully. Credit inside a tight cluster counts for nothing, like pigment that only shows on the outer willow bark, not the inner rings. A Sybil operator must win real trust from strangers outside its atlas of clones, paying more in reputation and stake than any fake identity can earn back.
